title: Fridge Compartment Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The fresh-food compartment NTC sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription: E1 on Gorenje (and rebadged Hisense-Gorenje group) refrigerators indicates the fridge compartment temperature sensor reading is outside the valid range. The compressor will run on a fallback profile and set-point changes have no effect.

causes.cause: Loose connector at the main board
Wire chafe inside the door hinge

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes and reconnect to clear transient faults.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Access the main board (typically rear lower panel). Reseat the sensor harness.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the NTC and measure ~5 kOhm at 25 C. Replace if open or shorted.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement NTC clipped at the original location.

whenToCallPro: If wiring is damaged inside the foamed-in liner.

faq.a: Cooling continues at a default rate but is not regulated - use a thermometer to monitor.

title: Freezer Compartment Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The freezer compartment NTC is out of range.
fullDescription: E2 reports failure of the freezer NTC. Without a valid freezer reading the controller cannot regulate compressor run time, leading to soft frozen foods or icy buildup.

causes.cause: Damaged wire inside the freezer liner

symptoms: Soft ice cream or partially thawed frozen food
Heavy frost in some areas, none in others

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the freezer NTC, measure ~16 kOhm at -10 C. Replace if open or shorted.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement and reroute harness clear of the evaporator.

whenToCallPro: If access requires removing the rear evaporator panel and you are uncomfortable with that.

faq.a: Frozen items will gradually thaw or accumulate frost - resolve quickly.

title: Evaporator Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The evaporator coil thermistor is open or shorted.
fullDescription: E3 indicates the evaporator-mounted thermistor used to terminate defrost is reading invalid. Frost may build up because the controller cannot terminate defrost optimally.

causes.cause: Connector unplugged after a previous repair

symptoms: Heavy frost on the rear freezer panel

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Empty contents and unplug for 24 hours.

fixSteps.title: Access evaporator
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear freezer panel screws.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement NTC clipped to the suction line and reroute harness.

whenToCallPro: If you cannot remove the rear freezer panel without flexing the liner.

faq.q: Why is frost building so quickly?
faq.a: Without an evaporator NTC the defrost cycle does not terminate properly, allowing frost to accumulate.

title: Defrost System Failure
shortDescription: Defrost timeout - heater or bimetal failed.
fullDescription: E4 is logged when the defrost cycle does not terminate within the maximum allowed time. The controller energizes the defrost heater but does not see the bimetal open, indicating a failed heater, bimetal, or thermal fuse.

causes.cause: Failed defrost relay on main board

symptoms: Heavy frost on rear of freezer

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 24 hours, towels at base.

fixSteps.title: Test heater
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance across heater. Open = replace. Typical 25-50 Ohm.

fixSteps.title: Test bimetal
fixSteps.instruction: Place in freezer 15 minutes; should close cold, open at room temp.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed parts
fixSteps.instruction: Install new heater and/or bimetal as identified.

whenToCallPro: If both components test good but E4 returns - main board defrost relay is suspect.

faq.q: Can I run the fridge with E4?
faq.a: Briefly - but cooling will degrade as frost accumulates.

title: Evaporator Fan Failure
shortDescription: The freezer evaporator fan is not running at expected speed.
fullDescription: E5 reports loss of tach feedback from the BLDC evaporator fan. Without circulation, both compartments warm despite the compressor running.
symptoms: Loud chirp that stops when the door opens

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 24 hours to clear ice.

fixSteps.title: Spin test
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear freezer panel, spin blade by hand - should rotate freely.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Install matching BLDC fan motor and reattach panel.

whenToCallPro: If ice keeps reforming after replacement - root cause is in the defrost system.

faq.q: Why is one side warmer than the other?
faq.a: Without the evaporator fan, cold air does not circulate evenly between compartments.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: User interface and main control board are not communicating.
fullDescription: E6 indicates serial communication between the display PCB and the main board has been lost. Cooling typically continues at the last commanded set point but settings cannot be changed.

causes.cause: Loose ribbon cable in the upper hinge

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open upper hinge cap and reseat the ribbon cable to the main board.

fixSteps.title: Replace boards
fixSteps.instruction: Replace UI first; if E6 persists, replace main board.

whenToCallPro: If main board needs to be replaced.

faq.a: Usually yes - main board keeps cooling at last set point.

title: Ambient Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The ambient temperature sensor is out of range.
fullDescription: Gorenje uses an ambient sensor to bias defrost and compressor logic. E7 means the controller cannot read this sensor; cooling continues but efficiency may suffer.
symptoms: Excessive run time in cool weather

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the ambient sensor (often near the main board) and reseat.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure ~5 kOhm at 25 C. Replace if shorted or open.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new ambient NTC.

faq.a: No, but efficiency may drop in extreme room temperatures.

title: Damper Motor Fault (Multi-Air-Flow Models)
shortDescription: The air damper between freezer and fridge compartments is not moving.
fullDescription: On Gorenje multi-air-flow models a stepper-driven damper regulates cold air to the fridge compartment. E8 indicates the controller has lost feedback on the damper position - typically a stuck or failed damper assembly.
symptoms: Fridge too warm while freezer is correct

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 24 hours to free any ice on the damper.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the damper at the top of the fridge compartment; reseat the connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace damper
fixSteps.instruction: Install matching damper assembly with motor.

whenToCallPro: If the damper assembly is integrated with ductwork that requires partial cabinet disassembly.

faq.a: Yes - the damper only controls cold-air flow into the fresh-food compartment.

title: Power Failure Notification
shortDescription: The refrigerator detected a recent power outage.
fullDescription: PF is informational - the refrigerator was unpowered for some period. Verify food safety and dismiss the alert.
symptoms: PF on display when powered back up

fixSteps.title: Acknowledge alarm
fixSteps.instruction: Press the alarm/mute button to dismiss PF.

fixSteps.title: Verify food safety
fixSteps.instruction: Discard items above 40 F for over 4 hours; refreeze those still containing ice crystals.

fixSteps.title: Inspect outlet
fixSteps.instruction: If PF appears repeatedly without outage, test outlet voltage and inspect breaker.

whenToCallPro: If PF appears with no real outages.

faq.a: Most Gorenje models do not allow disabling - it protects food safety.

title: Door Open Alarm
shortDescription: A door has been left open longer than the alarm timeout.
fullDescription: dO triggers after about 2 minutes with the door switch reading open. The interior light flashes and the unit beeps until the door is closed.

fixSteps.title: Close all doors firmly
fixSteps.instruction: Push doors closed, verify gasket seals around the perimeter.

fixSteps.title: Check obstructions
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure shelves and items are seated and not preventing closure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect gasket
fixSteps.instruction: Replace torn or deformed gasket.

fixSteps.title: Test door switch
fixSteps.instruction: Use a multimeter to verify the reed switch toggles. Replace if stuck.

faq.a: The alarm/mute button silences the audible beep but dO remains until the door is closed.
